entities.summary: Australia is a sovereign nation in Australia and New Zealand, Oceania. Its capital is Canberra. Official languages include English (de facto). Government: Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy. Population: approximately 26.7 million. Area: 7,692,024 km². Comprehensive index for Australia covering Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples (65,000+ years continuous habitation, oldest living cultures on Earth), Dutch exploration (1606 Janszoon, 'New Holland'), British colonisation (1770 Cook, 1788 First Fleet/Botany Bay, penal colony), frontier wars and dispossession, six colonies federated 1901 (Commonwealth of Australia), White Australia Policy (1901-1973, Immigration Restriction Act), Gallipoli 1915 (ANZAC legend, national myth), WWII (Darwin bombing, Kokoda, Pacific War alliance with US), post-war immigration boom (Mediterranean/European, multiculturalism), Whitlam dismissal 1975 (constitutional crisis), reconciliation movement, Stolen Generations apology 2008 (Rudd), 2023 Voice referendum failed, AUKUS alliance.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Australia's history of dispossession and frontier wars had a profound impact on Indigenous Australians, with estimates suggesting up to 90% of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples died due to violence, disease, and forced relocation. The country's colonial past continues to shape its contemporary identity.
